extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients, principal investigators, and institutional research administrators preparing RPPRs
extracted.subtask_description: Completing the NIH Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) Sections A–I (and supplemental instructions) to meet NIH/AHRQ reporting, compliance, and budget requirements for ongoing grants. Includes human subjects, vertebrate animals, clinical trials, foreign disclosures, budget forms, and outcomes reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: F.3.b Vertebrate Animals — report significant changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are or will be significant changes to the uses of vertebrate animals from the previous submission, provide a description of the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of significant changes include, but are not limited to, changing animal species, changing from noninvasive to invasive procedures, new project/performance site(s) where animals will be used, etc. If studies involving live vertebrate animals are planned and were not part of the originally proposed research design, provide a new or revised Vertebrate Animal Section as described in the competing application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: F.3.c Biohazards — report differences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the use of biohazards is or will be different from that in the previous submission, provide a description and explanation of the difference(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: F.3.d Select Agents — report changes and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the possession, use, or transfer of Select Agents is or will be different from that proposed in the previous submission, provide a description and explanation of the differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include changes in select agent research location and/or required level of biocontainment. If the use of Select Agents was proposed previously but has not been approved by regulatory authorities, provide an explanation. If studies involving Select Agents are planned and were not part of the originally proposed research design, provide a description of proposed use, possession, transfer, and research location as described in competing application instructions. (Link: U.S. Select Agent Registry)

rubrics_metrics.name: Section G — address award-specific reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPR Section G addresses agency-specific award terms and conditions and any award specific reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to special reporting requirements specified in the Notice of Award (NoA) or Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). See supplemental instructions for specific grant RPPR types.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.1 MFTRP certification for senior/key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: For RPPRs submitted on or after January 25, 2026, senior/key personnel must certify annually regarding participation or non-participation in a Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program (MFTRP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a flattened PDF in Section G.1 with language: 'I [insert name] certify that, at the time of submission, I am not a party to a malign foreign talent recruitment program.' File must be named 'MFTRPcert_[Name].pdf'. See NOT-OD-26-018.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.1 NRSA childcare costs reporting (training awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: For NRSA Institutional Training Awards, provide an attachment specifying the number of trainees who used childcare costs in the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Supplemental Instructions for Training RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.1 SBIR/STTR Life Cycle Certifications (I-RPPR/F-RPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR recipients must submit Life Cycle Certifications within Interim and Final RPPR in Section G.1; forms must be uploaded directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not select 'Nothing to Report' for this section. The I-RPPR or F-RPPR will not be accepted unless all completed Life Cycle Certification(s) are received. Forms are available in fillable format at the SBIR/STTR forms directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.1 SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Form update requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR recipients must address whether changes require submission of an updated Required Disclosures of Foreign Affiliations or Relationships to Foreign Countries form as part of Annual, Interim, and Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes are indicated, submit an updated SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Form via the Foreign Disclosure Request for Additional Materials (RAM) feature in eRA Commons. Updated forms must have all questions addressed, be signed, and submitted as a flattened PDF. See eRA Commons Online Help.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.4 Human Subjects — cumulative enrollment and inclusion reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If conducting NIH-defined clinical research, report cumulative enrollment of subjects and distribution by sex, race, and ethnicity as defined in competing application instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inclusion enrollment progress or cumulative enrollment doesn't reflect planned enrollment, address reasons in Section F.3.a. Update inclusion enrollment with total cumulative data on the inclusion enrollment report(s) for each study record in the Human Subjects System (HSS). If last competing application submitted Jan 25, 2019 or later, submit deidentified individual-level participant data using the HSS spreadsheet template. Inclusion enrollment updates must be submitted prior to RPPR submission; warnings occur if not updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.4 AHRQ-specific inclusion enrollment instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: AHRQ recipients: if inclusion enrollment reporting is required, complete and upload the Cumulative Inclusion Enrollment Report in Section G.4; if not required, select 'Nothing to Report.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for collecting race and ethnicity data (OMB Directive No. 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use OMB Directive No. 15 categories and definitions for ethnicity and race for NIH reporting purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethnic categories: Hispanic or Latino; Not Hispanic or Latino. Racial categories: American Indian or Alaska Native; Asian; Black or African American; Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander; White. These are social-political constructs for federal reporting and should be used to allow comparisons to federal databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect race/ethnicity by self-identification and two-question format
rubrics_metrics.description: When collecting data on ethnicity and race, use self-identification and the OMB-recommended two-question format (ethnicity first, then race) and allow selecting more than one race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIH inclusion enrollment format is not a data collection instrument — collect data with study instruments and use that information to complete NIH forms. Report participants who self-identify with more than one race in the 'More Than One Race' category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting/reporting subpopulations — aggregatability
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouraged to collect greater detail on ethnic/racial subpopulations when relevant, provided additional categories can be aggregated into OMB categories for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide subpopulation details in the Comments field of inclusion enrollment forms and/or text of progress report when available and relevant to scientific questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. populations — culturally appropriate collection and separate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For NIH-defined clinical research outside the U.S., design culturally appropriate instruments for self-identification, but use OMB categories for reporting to NIH. Report non-U.S. site enrollment on a separate inclusion enrollment form from U.S. sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NIH Inclusion policy page or contact the program officer for additional guidance and FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting age at enrollment — deidentified participant-level data (.csv)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients who submitted the last competing application Jan 25, 2019 or later must include deidentified data on sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and age at enrollment for each study participant in .csv format using the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age may be reported in units ranging from minutes to years. See tip sheet and video for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to planned enrollment — contact program officer and revise records
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are changes from the planned enrollment originally approved for funding, contact the program officer and revise the existing Planned Enrollment record in the Human Subjects System; address the change in Section F.3.a of the RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III clinical trials — reporting cumulative enrollment and analysis status
rubrics_metrics.description: For NIH-defined Phase III Clinical Trials, report cumulative enrollment and indicate in Section F.3.a whether any data analysis has begun; if analysis started or data published, report progress in evaluating potential differences by sex, race, and/or ethnicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per law, entities conducting Phase III trials must include results of valid analyses by sex, race, and ethnicity in addition to submission in ClinicalTrials.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT requirement within 21 days of first enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies involving clinical trials must provide the ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT) in Section 1 of the HSCT form within 21 days of enrollment of the first participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may use the 'populate' button to bring forward data from ClinicalTrials.gov once the NCT is entered. RPPR submission will be blocked with an error if trials subject to FDAAA/NIH dissemination policy are past registration deadlines and no NCT is entered. To address the error, provide the NCT or upload the ClinicalTrials.gov registration receipt to HSCT other attachments as CTgov_Registration_Receipt.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Milestone Plan completion and date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must complete Section 6 – Clinical Trial Milestone Plan for all studies involving clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All anticipated dates entered must be future dates. All actual dates must be the current date or a later date. Some dates (e.g., Study Start Date when set to 'actual') cannot be modified once set to actual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of trial dates and enrollment milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific dates: Study Primary Completion Date; Study Final Completion Date; Enrollment milestones (first participant, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% of planned enrollment); Completion of primary endpoint analyses; Reporting of results in ClinicalTrials.gov; indicate whether the trial is applicable under FDAAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each date entered must be marked anticipated or actual. Study Primary Completion Date refers to final participant examined/received intervention for primary outcome; Final Completion Date refers to final collection for primary and secondary outcomes and adverse events. Some actual dates cannot be modified once set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials reporting compliance — results due under FDAAA/NIH policy
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPR submission will be prevented if associated clinical trials have results due under FDAAA and/or NIH Policy and results have not been submitted to ClinicalTrials.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To resolve the error submit results to ClinicalTrials.gov or upload the submission receipt for a Good Cause extension request or Certification of Delayed Submission of Results Information as CTgov_Extension_Receipt.pdf in HSCT attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.5 Human Subjects Education Requirement — newly involved personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: If personnel are newly involved in the design or conduct of human subjects research, provide their names, the title of the human subjects education program completed by each individual, and a one-sentence description of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.6 Human Embryonic Stem Cells (hESC) — use and registry requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project involves human embryonic stem cells, only hESC lines listed as approved in the NIH Registry may be used in NIH-funded research; identify NIH Registry numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a change in the use of hESCs provide an explanation. Use the 'Add hESC Number' button to add data to the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.7 Vertebrate Animals — indicate involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the project involves vertebrate animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.8 Project/Performance Sites — update and assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are changes to project/performance site(s), edit as appropriate and designate one site as the Primary Performance Site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including a new site where human subjects or vertebrate animals will be involved, address the change under F.3.a or F.3.b. If a site is engaged in human subjects research, the recipient organization must ensure the site operates under an appropriate Federal Wide Assurance and complies with 45 CFR Part 46 and NIH policies. For vertebrate animals, ensure all sites hold OLAW-approved Assurances; if recipient lacks animal program and work will be at another organization with an Assurance, the recipient must obtain an Assurance from OLAW prior to involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.9 Foreign component — identify and describe
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide organization name, country, and description of each foreign component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign component is defined as significant scientific activity performed outside the United States by the recipient or a researcher employed by a foreign organization, whether or not grant funds were expended. Significant activities that must be reported include involvement of human subjects or live vertebrate animals; extensive foreign travel by project staff to collect data; any activity that may impact U.S. foreign policy. Examples: collaborations anticipated to result in co-authorship; use of facilities or instrumentation at a foreign site; receipt of financial support or resources from a foreign entity. Foreign travel for consultation does not meet the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.10 Estimated unobligated balance — >25% reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether estimated unobligated balance (including prior year carryover) will be greater than 25% of the current year's total approved budget; if yes, provide the estimated unobligated balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total approved budget = current fiscal year award authorization plus any approved carryover. Numerator = total amount available for carryover; denominator = current year's total approved budget. AHRQ has different calculation rules (automatic 'yes' and does not include approved carryover). If >25%, provide explanation in G.10.b. If authorized to carryover, provide a general description of how funds will be spent in G.10.c. Recipients not authorized to carryover must submit a prior approval request to the awarding IC per NIH Grants Policy Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.11 Program Income — anticipated income reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether program income is anticipated during the next budget period; if yes, provide amount and source(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program income = gross income earned by recipient/consortium/contractor under the grant directly generated by grant-supported activity (examples: fees for services, charges for use/rental of property/equipment, sale of commodities, registration fees, license fees/royalties). Program income from license fees and royalties is exempt from reporting unless otherwise specified in award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.12 F&A Costs (SNAP awards) — site changes affecting F&A
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a change in performance sites that will affect Facilities & Administrative (F&A) costs for SNAP awards, provide an explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: H.1 Budget Form — SF424 R&R and justification for significant rebudgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the SF424 Research & Related Budget and follow competing application instructions (Section G.300 R&R Budget Form) to complete R&R sections A–L and the R&R Cumulative Budget. Upload budget justification as Item L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget justification must include detailed justification for line items and amounts that represent a significant change from previously recommended levels (e.g., total re-budgeting greater than 25% of the total award amount for this budget period). AHRQ recipients: total costs should not exceed NoA committed level. Include detailed consortia budgets in H.2 if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward budgets — manual calculation of main budget F.5
rubrics_metrics.description: If subaward budgets are completed, the system will not calculate budget line item F.5 for the main budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total consortium costs for the main budget MUST be computed and entered manually into budget line item F.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: H.2 Subaward Budget Form — use SF424 R&R Subaward Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards with subaward/consortium budgets, select the SF424 Research & Related Subaward Budget from the dropdown and follow Subaward Budget Attachment(s) Form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: I.1 Outcomes — public summary and interim/final RPPR requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information regarding cumulative outcomes or findings of the project; for NIH Section I outcomes will be made publicly available and length should not exceed half a page for NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interim or final RPPR, the summary must be: written for the general public in clear, concise, and comprehensible language; suitable for electronic dissemination; and must not include proprietary, confidential information, or trade secrets. See samples of acceptable project outcomes. Per law, Phase III trials must include results of valid analyses by sex/gender, race, and ethnicity in addition to ClinicalTrials.gov submission. This section applies only to Interim and Final RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include sensitive PII or PHI in the RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR must not include Sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or Protected Health Information (PHI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive PII examples: Social Security Number, personal financial information, Alien Registration Number. PHI examples: personal medical conditions. Documents containing sensitive PII or PHI must not be included in the RPPR. NIH Grants recipients: see FAQ or IC Privacy Coordinator for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: K awards — B.4 training/professional development reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe opportunities for training and professional development provided by the project, indicating percent of time spent in each activity and relationship to the recipient's research career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mentored career development awards (e.g., K00, K01, K22, K99), indicate whether the organization uses Individual Development Plans (IDPs) and describe how they were used during the reporting period (do not include actual IDP). For awards that require mentoring others (e.g., K05, K24), indicate percent time devoted to mentoring, individuals mentored, frequency and kinds of mentoring, financial and other support to mentees, and productivity of mentoring relationships. AHRQ recipients: some items may be Not Applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: K awards — B.6 plans for next reporting period and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline for activities planned for the next year, including plans to apply for subsequent grant support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients of transition awards should report progress in identifying an independent research position. Recipients charged with mentoring should describe planned mentoring activities and proposed mentees (backgrounds, interests, professional levels) sufficient to evaluate mentoring quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: K awards — C.5.c Data Management and Sharing applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) requirements apply for career awards for competing applications submitted on or after January 25, 2023, except as noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not applicable for K12, KL1, and KM1. See NIH activity codes subject to DMS policy and NIH Scientific Data Sharing website for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: K awards — G.2 Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the RCR instruction received (or instruction given) during this reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address five components: Format, Subject Matter, Faculty Participation, Duration, and Frequency. Additional detailed guidance is in competing application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: K awards — G.3 Mentor's Report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For mentored K awards, provide a mentor-signed PDF letter assessing the recipient's progress and performance during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessment of research progress and development toward independence, and information on continued mentor commitment. Letter must be signed and uploaded.
